findings.claim: The Ten Obligatory Acts "include all of the Five Pillars (Salah, Sawm, Zakah, Hajj and Jihad) plus five additional duties"; the glossary and the inline definition repeat that they "include the Five Pillars".
findings.truth: The Ten Obligatory Acts (furu ad-din) are Salah, Sawm, Zakah, Khums, Hajj, jihad, Amr bil ma'ruf, Nahi anil munkar, Tawalla and Tabarra. They contain four of the Five Pillars, not five: the Shahadah is not among them. Jihad is not a Pillar of Sunni Islam.
findings.evidence: spec 3.1.5.2 (Five Pillars of Sunni Islam and the Ten Obligatory Acts of Shi'a Islam); the lesson's own list at n8 gives the correct ten and omits Shahadah

findings.claim: Revision tip: "list the five extra Obligatory Acts that Shi'a Muslims follow beyond the Five Pillars".
findings.truth: Six of the Ten sit outside the Five Pillars: Khums, jihad, Amr bil ma'ruf, Nahi anil munkar, Tawalla and Tabarra.
findings.evidence: recount of the lesson's own list at n8

findings.claim: Surah 112 quoted as "He is Allah, the One, Allah is Eternal and Absolute. None is born of Him, He is unborn. There is none like unto Him."
findings.truth: That wording appears in no standard translation. Abdel Haleem, the translation used elsewhere in this unit, reads: "Say, 'He is God the One, God the eternal. He begot no one nor was He begotten. No one is comparable to Him.'"
findings.evidence: api.quran.com translation 85 (Abdel Haleem), chapter 112; Wikipedia Al-Ikhlas for Sahih International, Yusuf Ali and Pickthall

findings.claim: Q2 is typed "1 mark - Give/Name" but asks for two acts and its scheme awards "1 mark for each, up to 2 marks"; the accepted list also omits jihad.
findings.truth: Each religion is examined by two five-part questions of 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks, so no 2-mark question exists on this paper. Jihad is one of the Ten Obligatory Acts and is not a Pillar, so it must be accepted.

findings.claim: Q4 model answer: "Surah 112 declares Allah is 'One, Eternal and Absolute.'"
findings.truth: Not verbatim in a standard translation. Abdel Haleem gives "He is God the One" and "No one is comparable to Him".

findings.claim: Q5 model answer: "It affirms Tawhid, which the Qur'an calls the most fundamental belief (Surah 112)."
findings.truth: Surah 112 states God's oneness and uniqueness. It makes no ranking claim about which belief is most fundamental, so the attribution is invented.

findings.claim: Qur'an 2:163 quoted as "Your God is one God. There is no deity except Him, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful".
findings.truth: A hybrid: "There is no deity except Him" is Sahih International (which brackets "[worthy of worship]"), while "the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful" is Khattab's Clear Quran. Abdel Haleem reads "Your God is the one God: there is no god except Him, the Lord of Mercy, the Giver of Mercy." Reference and meaning are correct, so no marks are at risk.

findings.claim: Q2 is typed "1 mark - Give/Name" but asks for two groups and awards "1 mark for each, up to 2 marks".
findings.truth: The five parts are worth 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks. There is no 2-mark question on this paper.

findings.claim: "examiners reward students who can explain why each ritual is performed, not just what happens".
findings.truth: A fabricated examiner claim. The advice itself is sound and survives without the invented attribution.
findings.evidence: house rule: no invented examiner or mark-scheme claims

findings.claim: Hajj "attracts over two million Muslims from around the world each year".
findings.truth: Recorded attendance was 1,845,045 (2023), 1,833,164 (2024) and 1,673,230 (2025). Only 2019 (2,489,406) passed two million. "More than 1.5 million" is safe for every recent year.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Hajj, official Saudi pilgrim table

findings.claim: Q4 model answer: "Over two million Muslims from every nation stand together at Arafat".
findings.truth: Same stale figure as F10; the model answer must match the corrected text.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Hajj, official Saudi pilgrim table

findings.claim: Q2 is typed "1 mark - Give/Name" but asks for two rituals and awards "1 mark for each, up to 2 marks".
findings.truth: The five parts are worth 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks. There is no 2-mark question on this paper.

findings.claim: Q6 "Explain two ways in which the rituals of Hajj connect Muslims to the Prophet Ibrahim." is typed "4 marks - Explain Similarities & Differences".
findings.truth: The question asks for two ways, not a comparison. Two house labels already exist in this board's corpus for that stem: "4 marks - Explain Influence" (16 uses, all "Explain two ways in which...") and "4 marks - Explain" (4 uses). Choosing between them is a corpus-wide labelling call, so it belongs with the question-type relabel programme rather than this unit.
findings.ruling: Leave (fleet-wide RS relabel / spec publishes no split).

findings.claim: "Examiners specifically look for the conditions that must be met before lesser jihad can be declared".
findings.truth: A fabricated examiner claim. The instruction to learn three conditions with Qur'anic support stands on its own.
findings.evidence: house rule: no invented examiner or mark-scheme claims

findings.claim: Q2 is typed "1 mark - Give/Name" but asks for two conditions and awards "1 mark for each, up to 2 marks".
findings.truth: The five parts are worth 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks. There is no 2-mark question on this paper.

findings.claim: Q4 model answer states "The Prophet Muhammad himself described the inner struggle as the 'greater' jihad" and offers that hadith as the source.
findings.truth: The lesson text itself explains that this hadith is graded weak and is absent from the six authoritative collections. The model answer drops that caveat. AQA accepts the hadith as a source, so no marks are at risk, but the two passages contradict each other.

findings.claim: At Mina "pilgrims throw pebbles at three stone pillars".
findings.truth: The three pillars were replaced by long walls (the Jamarat) after 2004 to reduce crushing. GCSE textbooks still say pillars and the symbolism is unchanged, so no marks are at risk.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia Stoning of the Devil / Jamarat Bridge

findings.claim: Every 4-mark question in the unit is typed "4 marks - Explain Similarities & Differences", a stem the spec prescribes for the thematic studies section rather than the study-of-religions section.
findings.truth: The spec's contrasting-belief wording sits under the themes, but the Islam content requires "common and divergent views within Islam" and "key differences in the practice of salah in Sunni and Shi'a Islam", so comparison questions are legitimate practice for this section. Only the marks and the paper structure are spec-fixed; stems are not.

summary: Doctrine is largely sound: the Qur'anic references, Sunni and Shi'a prayer counts, khums, the zakah rate and nisab, the Hajj sequence and the Ashura attributions all check out. The costly errors are the claim that the Ten Obligatory Acts contain all Five Pillars (they omit the Shahadah and jihad is not a Pillar), a Surah 112 quotation in wording no translation uses, and a 2-mark award on all four second-part questions when this paper has none.
